output.question: Has General Motors announced layoffs?

passages.quote: General Motors has announced plans to lay off 361 workers employed at assembly and stamping plants in Lansing.
We anticipate recalling affected employees back to Lansing Grand River at the end of the retooling period
As part of that work, we have made the difficult decision to eliminate certain roles globally.
The global reductions began Monday and will impact about 500 to 600 employees

output.answer: Yes. As of November 11, 2026, the most recent announcement verified was reported on August 14: General Motors planned to lay off hundreds of workers at its Lansing assembly and stamping plants in January 2027 during retooling, with recalls expected afterward. Earlier, on May 11, 2026, GM confirmed global IT job cuts; CNBC reported that approximately 500–600 salaried employees would be affected.
caveats: Reports disagree on the precise Lansing headcount and effective day: WILX reported 350 employees and January 14, 2027, while MLive reported 361 and January 17, 2027. GM anticipated recalls after retooling, so these should not be described as confirmed permanent job losses.
The 500–600 IT-job estimate came from CNBC’s unnamed source; GM confirmed the cuts but declined to provide specific details.
missing_fields: Definitive Lansing headcount and exact effective day verified against the original WARN notice.

key_facts.fact: GM announced layoffs affecting hundreds of employees at Lansing Grand River Assembly/Stamping and Lansing Regional Stamping, scheduled for January 2027 during retooling.
GM said it anticipated recalling affected employees to Lansing Grand River after the retooling period.
GM confirmed global IT job cuts. CNBC reported approximately 500–600 affected salaried employees, largely in Austin, Texas, and Warren, Michigan, citing a person familiar with the plans.

citations.title: GM lays off 500-600 salaried IT workers to cut costs
excerpts: DETROIT – [General Motors](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/GM/) is laying off hundreds of salaried employees in its information technology operations as the automaker reevaluates its workforce needs and cuts costs, CNBC has learned. The global reductions began Monday and will impact about 500 to 600 employees, largely in Austin, Texas, and Warren, Michigan, according to a person familiar with the plans who was not authorized to speak publicly about the layoffs. GM confirmed the cuts, which were first reported by [Bloomberg News,](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-11/gm-to-cut-hundreds-of-white-collar-workers-in-push-to-trim-costs?srnd=homepage-americas) but declined to give specific details about the actions. “GM is transforming its Information Technology organization to better position the company for the future. As part of that work, we have made the difficult decision to eliminate certain roles globally. We are grateful for the contributions of the employees affected and are committed to supporting them through this transition,” the automaker said in an emailed statement.

CNBC establishes GM’s confirmation of global IT cuts and the separately attributed estimate of 500–600 salaried employees.
